newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Standard Bank unveils forex account plans.
newsitem.headline: Standard Bank unveils forex account plans.

text.p: South Africa's Standard Bank Investment Corp on Tuesday unveiled its foreign currency deposit account and offshore unit trust fund products, which it plans to offer after the relaxation of exchange controls on July 1.

"Standard Bank is in a unique position as we can offer our clients foreign currency deposit accounts both in South Africa or overseas, though our offshore operations in Jersey and the Isle of Man," retail banking managing director Noel Webb said in a statement.
South African residents will be able to hold foreign currency accounts for the first time from July 1, subject to central bank limits which are yet to be announced.

Standard Bank's Customer Foreign Currency Resident Account (CFC) would enable South Africans to invest on call or for terms up to 12 months in locally held accounts denominated in U.S. dollars, German marks, Japanese yen, British pounds and Swiss Francs.
Standard said customers would be able to invest in more than one type of currency within the same account. A minimum 10,000 rand balance would be required
"One of the benefits of a CFC account is that it acts as a rand hedge. The interest rate varies, depending on the currency and is based on the London Interbank Bid Rate (Libid)," it said.
The bank also offered an offshore call account based in Jersey and the Isle of Man for U.S. dollar, sterling, rand and German mark deposits.
Standard bank said it would also offer offshore trusts comprising six equity, two bond and four currency funds.

The equity funds would invest in the United States, Europe, the United Kingdom, South East Asia, Japan and other international markets while the bond funds would invest in U.K. gilts and other international debt.
The currency funds included German mark, sterling, Swiss Franc and U.S. dollar denominations.
